top_signal.title: GitHub Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
top_signal.summary: GitHub’s Copilot code review adds approval assessments and, when enabled by admins, can submit approvals that count toward a repository’s required-approvals rule. Feature is off by default and offered in public preview to paid plans.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Automated approvals alter who (or what) can satisfy merge gates — QA leads must review policy controls, path restrictions, and auditability before enabling approvals.

items.title: Mantis: Google publishes an open-source harness to find, reproduce and fix bugs
items.summary: Google open-sourced Mantis, an agentic harness that combines critic/review agents with sandboxed reproduction to improve true-positive rates, repository-aware context, and automated patch suggestions for discovered vulnerabilities.
items.why_it_matters: QA and QA-security teams can adopt Mantis patterns to reproduce findings reliably, reduce false positives, and integrate agentic discovery into verification workflows and pipelines.

items.title: CLion adds an AI skill to decode and triage hard faults in embedded projects
items.summary: CLion 2026.2.2 ships clion-embedded-hardfault: an MCP-backed AI skill that decodes fault registers, inspects memory/disassembly, and traces the root cause across debug probes and vendor tools.
items.why_it_matters: Embedded QA can speed failure triage and verification: agents produce actionable root-cause evidence and can re-run debug checks as part of automated test flows.

items.title: Copilot app and CLI now honor enterprise content exclusions
items.summary: GitHub made content-exclusion policies generally available in the Copilot app and CLI so enterprise-configured exclusions aren’t used as model context for suggestions and reviews.
items.why_it_matters: Protects sensitive test fixtures, proprietary code, and PII in repositories from being used as AI context — important for test-data governance and compliance in automated QA workflows.

items.title: Android Studio Quail 4: Gemma 4 and Android skills for test generation and developer flows
items.summary: Android Studio Quail 4 (stable) integrates Gemma 4 Android skills and Android-specific AI features intended to speed development and create AI-assisted test workflows within the IDE.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile QA engineers should evaluate generated test cases, emulator flows, and device-coverage impacts; validate generated tests and guard against brittle or unsafe test artifacts.

items.title: Automating the experimentation lifecycle with Kiro, AWS DevOps Agent, and LaunchDarkly
items.summary: AWS DevOps Blog demonstrates automating experiment lifecycles by combining Kiro, the AWS DevOps Agent, and LaunchDarkly to detect events, apply validated changes, and open PRs for human review.
items.why_it_matters: QA can automate experiment validation and evidence collection, tying feature-flag experiments to reproducible verification steps and gating rollouts on test/evidence outcomes.

watch.title: TeamCity 2026.2: pipelines GA and AI assistant integrations worth monitoring
watch.category: CI quality gates / Agentic QA orchestration
watch.summary: TeamCity 2026.2 moves pipeline features out of EAP and introduces AI-related extensions (including BYOK for AI Assistant) that affect pipeline design and agent tooling integration.
watch.why_it_matters: Watch for changes that affect how QA gates, approvals, and agent-driven test tooling are wired into CI pipelines and enterprise policy controls.

learning.title: MPS 2026.2 EAP: flexible result matching and clearer editor test failures
learning.summary: MPS 2026.2 EAP adds flexible result matching for editor tests and more informative failure messages, reducing brittle assertions and making failures point to the offending node and cell.
learning.why_it_matters: Study flexible result matching to reduce brittle tests and speed triage; practical technique for making GUI/editor tests more resilient and maintainable.
